thread:
marta: seeing a 2x p99 increase from frankfurt-pop since 11:30 UTC, affects small-seq workloads only. graphs show tail latency spike around kernel handoff windows. anyone else?
ryan: yup I've been watching it, looks correlated with kernel selection stage in the runtime. fallback path to scalar kernels spikes CPU and latency.
akshay: interesting — did batching changes land on that pop yesterday? I pushed an adaptive-window heuristic tweak early morning.
marta: yes akshay's change landed at 03:12 UTC to reduce batch-window for short sequences. maybe the heuristics are causing more kernel churn.
ci-bot: deploy 2026-04-17T03:12 by akshay passed smoke checks.
leah: ops: net metrics look stable (no carrier issues). traceroutes from frankfurt show consistent AS path. DNS resolved fine.
samir: grabbed a CPU/kern profile from a host during spike. attaching snippet:
```
# top kernels by time
kernel_select_policy::evaluate 42%
run_kernel(CUDA_fp16_conv) 3%
run_kernel(SCALAR_fallback) 38%
KVCache::evict 10%
batcher::dispatch 7%
```
marta: that % for scalar fallback is alarming. suggests kernel selection is flipping to fallback for lots of short requests.
ryan: could be due to micro-variations in seq length distribution after the batching tweak — short noisy tenant causing tiny batches that don't qualify for optimized kernels.
akshay: I can roll back the adaptive-window tweak or tighten the eligibility checks for optimized kernels. which is faster?
leah: rollback is fastest to test. but we should capture more profiling to confirm root cause before full rollback.
jun: also saw increased KV cache evictions on that pop. eviction rate jumped 3x during spikes — might be noisy neighbor causing cache churn.
samir: snapshot of KV metrics: hit_rate went from 0.92 -> 0.74 concurrent with latency spike. average prefix cache size per-worker decreased 30%.
opsbot: @oncall-frankfurt notified (incident P2). suggested mitigation: enable tenant isolation lanes and raise local cache quota for critical tenants.
marta: can we temporary-enable shard isolation for top 5 tenants and re-run perf tests?
ryan: yes I can enable isolation and pin their workloads to dedicated workers. doing it now.
ci-bot: isolation toggle applied to pop-frankfurt: lanes=5, quota=1.5x at 11:48 UTC.
akshay: after isolation the p99 dropped ~25% in the first 10m, still above baseline though.
leah: network still clean. looks like a combination: batching heuristic causing kernel churn + KV cache thrash from noisy tenant.
jun: long-term we should add a hysteresis to kernel selection so it doesn't flip on single-batch variance. also add eviction smoothing to KV cache metrics to avoid reactive thrashing.
marta: agree. action items: 1) akshay rollback or gate adaptive-window heuristics (short term) 2) ryan finish tenant isolation automation (short term) 3) samir & jun add kernel-selection hysteresis + eviction smoothing (next sprint) 4) leah monitor and reopen if p99 > baseline for 30m.
ryan: filing follow-up PR to add a min-stable-window param to kernel selection.
akshay: I'll open rollback PR and a feature-flag toggle for the adaptive-window.
leah: incident P2 -> degraded perf, mitigated with tenant isolation, monitoring. leaving open for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
marta: thanks team. please paste links to perf flamegraphs and the PRs here when ready.
ryan: https://ci.internal/reports/1771205432/flamegraph.svg
samir: PRs: https://git.internal/runtime/pulls/534 (rollback), https://git.internal/runtime/pulls/535 (hysteresis prototype)
jun: adding a short eval job against frankfurt-pop with synthetic short-seq workload to validate hysteresis changes. will post results in 30m.
marta: closing notes: new action item to add region-specific synthetic checks to catch kernel-selection regressions earlier.
